title: I built Basileia, an Early Byzantine city builder, as a solo dev using Claude Opus 5.5, Suno, and Godot
author: Extension-Animal8079
selftext:
Over the last few months I built Basileia, a chill city builder set in Early Byzantium, inspired by Caesar III and RollerCoaster Tycoon. 

Since this was a solo project, I leaned heavily on AI tools to make the scope manageable:

* **Code:** mostly Claude Code, from my design and playtests.
* **3D:** every building, ship and person was made by Claude in code. No model files and no 3D generators.
* **Trailer:** I directed the shots and the pacing. Claude scripted the cameras, recorded the footage in Godot and put picture and sound together with FFmpeg.
* **Art and sound:** maps and backgrounds made with Codex, music from Suno, some sound effects from ElevenLabs.

**Steam:** [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5637240/Basileia/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=r\_aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5637240/Basileia/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=r_aigamedev)

comments.author: Glaseng
comments.body: What was your dev approach here? Did you create a specific team of subagents, or just let Opus run free? How long did it take, and what subscription tier? Not meaning to interrogate, just wondering how much investment it takes to get something that actually resembles a real game.

replies.author: Extension-Animal8079
replies.body:
Mostly sequential prompting with Opus 5.5, and I rarely used subagent teams. Instead, I kept tight control over the design and took a very iterative approach, refining things like the 3D models step by step until I was happy with the result. I also brought in other tools where needed (Codex for 2D art, Gemini for text edits, Suno for music, and ElevenLabs for SFX).

It took almost 2 months of pretty intense work (10+ hours a day, and Claude worked overnight too) to get everything playable and polished.

As for the cost, I used the $100 Claude Code plan plus basic tiers for Codex, Suno, and ElevenLabs.

comments.author: Abyssalian
comments.body: Looks great! This reminds me a lot of the classic city-builders by Sierra and Impressions Games, like Caesar and Pharaoh. The models look quite procedurally generated when zooming in, which isn't an issue at all(!), though I definitely prefer the view from afar. Zoomed out, it looks really beautiful, and I can tell you spent a lot of time getting the details right. I can only imagine how long it must have taken to make walkers take an optimised path..

replies.author: Extension-Animal8079
replies.body:
Thanks a lot! Caesar III and Pharaoh were my main inspiration, so that means a lot.

You're right about the models. Every building and person is built in code, out of simple shapes. The game is meant to be played from a distance, like the old Impressions games, so that's where I put the work.

Polishing the walkers took a lot of work, especially the balance. To help with that, I built a bot that plays through missions and helped catch bugs and balance issues.
